correctness.rationale: Adding the antipodal maxima of the two disk support functions gives W=A+B+max(|A-B|,delta|Y|). The inequality W>=2max(A,B)>=sqrt(2(1+Y^2)) gives the four equality directions, and W<=2+delta with equality at the axial poles and no others for delta>0. On folding, y=|Y| is uniform on [0,1] and q=(1-y^2)|cos(2phi)|; its conditional arcsine density integrates to 1 and the joint density tends to 2/pi at (0,0). On the tail event, 2max(A,B) bounds y^2+q by sqrt(2) epsilon+epsilon^2/2. At y=sqrt(epsilon)v, q=epsilon s, the scaled width deficit is uniformly v^2/sqrt(2)+max(s/sqrt(2),lambda v)+O(epsilon) on the localized boxes. For lambda in [0,M], a narrow band about level 1 has vanishing area uniformly: the inequality involving s has slope 1/sqrt(2); in the other inequality, v^2/sqrt(2)+lambda v is increasing with derivative bounded below near 1 uniformly on this compact lambda range. The limiting event is 0<=v<u_lambda and 0<=s<sqrt(2)-v^2. Its area gives the stated profile after multiplication by 2/pi and normalization gives the conditional area law. At lambda=0, u=2^(1/4); at infinity u is asymptotic to 1/lambda. For fixed delta>0, W>=A+B+delta y and A+B>=sqrt(2)-O(epsilon^2) on the localized region give y=O_delta(epsilon). Scaling y and q both by epsilon gives a rectangle of area sqrt(2)/delta and the claimed coefficient and conditional law.
